questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Amoeba the              (i)             vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. In many cells, as in protists,           (ii)            vacuoles are formed by engulfing the particles.
questions.solution: In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the wrong statement
options: Bacteria cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan
Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells
Mycoplasma is a wall - less microorganism
questions.solution: Pili and fimbriae are surface structures of the bacteria that do not play a role in motility. Pili and fimbriae are elongated, hollow appendages seen in Gram-negative bacteria made of a unique protein, pilin. They serve in the attachment of bacteria with substratum and not in movement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which among the following can be seen in the ultrastructure of both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell?
questions.solution: The ribosomes are the smallest known electron microscopic without membrane, ribonucleoprotein particles attached either on RER or floating freely in the cytoplasm and are the sites of protein synthesis. Presence of ribosomes (size 23 nm in diameter) is revealed with the help of an electron microscope.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plastids that stores oils and fats are
questions.solution: In the chromoplasts fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present. This gives the part of the plant a yellow, orange, or red colour. The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If a subcellular fraction from liver tissue exhibits a high level of acid lipases, proteases, carbohydrases activity. The organelle associated with it will be
questions.solution: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cell wall consists of
options: Lignin, hemicellulose, pectin and lipid cellulose
questions.solution: Cell wall consists of lignin, hemicellulose, pectin and cellulose.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following cell organelles are enclosed by a single membrane?
questions.solution: Lysosomes are the unit membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus rich in hydrolytic enzymes like hydrolases, lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases, which are optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements:

i. Membrane-bounded inclusion bodies are not found in prokaryotic cells.
ii. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
iii. Pili are the surface structure of the bacteria which may play a role in motility.
iv. The cell membrane of prokaryotes is structurally similar to the eukaryotes.

Choose the option with the correct statements.
questions.solution: Pili are thin, hair-like appendages on the surface of bacteria. They are rigid in appearance than flagella, which have motility function.  Bacteria use sex pili for the process of conjugation. Pili also function as receptors for donor-specific (male-specific) phages.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following has the maximum % of the total cellular mass?
questions.solution:
Component and their % of the total cellular mass :

1. Water : 70-90 % 2. Proteins : 10-15 % 3. Nucleic acids : 5-7%

4. Carbohydrates : 3 % 5. Lipids : 2 % 6. Ions : 1%

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Choose an option with the correct statements from the list below.

i. The telomere is heterochromatic in nature.
ii. The acrocentric chromosome has centromere close to its end.
iii. Satellite is located near primary constriction.
iv. Submetacentric chromosomes are L-shaped.
questions.solution: The telocentric chromosome has centromere at the end of the chromosome and in the acrocentric chromosome, the centromere is near the end. These centromeres are present in the primary constriction and all chromosomes have primary constriction but some chromosomes during metaphase also show secondary constrictions that are called a satellite. They are present in some chromosome and help to identify the chromosome from others.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gas vacuoles are found in
questions.solution: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells is stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm, e.g., phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules. Gas vacuoles are found in blue-green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the organelles in column-I with their function in column-II and choose the correct option.

   Column I    Column II
(a) Golgi bodies (i) Helps in spindle formation
(b) RER (ii) Synthesis and storage of fats
(c) Microtubules (iii) Secretory proteins
(d) Sphaerosomes (iv) Helps in pseudopodia formation
    (v) Acrosome of sperms
questions.solution: The acrosome is a cap-like structure that is derived from the Golgi apparatus. Ribosomes bind to the endoplasmic reticulum and are called rough endoplasmic reticulum is involved in the formation of secretory proteins through translation mechanism. Microtubules help in spindle formation during cell division. Spherosomes or oleosomes are small cellular organelles with a single membrane responsible for the storage and synthesis of lipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who said 'all cells arise from pre-existing cells'?
questions.solution: In 1855, the German physiologist Rudolf Virchow added a third principle to the cell theory. Virchow stated that all cells arise from the division of pre-existing cells (Latin phrase "Omnis cellula e cellula").

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is true about ribosomes?
options: The prokaryotic ribosomes are 80S, where "S" stands for sedimentation differentiation.
These are composed of ribonucleic acid and proteins.
These are found only in eukaryotic cells.
These are self - splicing introns of some RNAs.
questions.solution: Ribosomes are amembraneous (i.e., without membrane) cell organelle composed of rRNA and protein. These are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. In prokaryotes, ribosomes are 70S type while in eukaryotes, it is 80S type. Here ‘S’ (Svedberg’s Unit) stands for the sedimentation coefficient.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the wrong statement from the following.
options: Both chloroplasts and mitochondria have an internal compartment, bounded by the thylakoid membrane.
Both chloroplasts and mitochondria contain DNA.
The chloroplasts are generally much larger than mitochondria.
Both chloroplasts and mitochondria contain an inner and an outer membrane.
questions.solution: Both chloroplasts and mitochondria contain DNA and are double membrane-bound organelles having an inner membrane and outer membrane. Mitochondria occur in the cytoplasm of both plants and animal cells. A mitochondrion contains two chambers. The inner membrane forms mitochondrial cristae. The chloroplast is also a double membranous organelle but found only in plants. The membrane-bound matrix of chloroplasts is stroma and inside the stroma thylakoids are present which form grana.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location. This gives the appearance of a small fragment called the
questions.solution: Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location. This gives the appearance of a small fragment called the satellite.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The enzyme used to join the DNA fragments is
questions.solution: DNA ligase is an enzyme used to join the DNA fragments. This enzyme catalyzes the formation of a covalent bond between adjacent 5' - P and 3' - OH termini in broken polynucleotide strands of dsDNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Microtubules are cylindrical structures having α and β tubulin proteins. They are the constituents of which one of the following groups?
questions.solution: Microtubules are microscopic hollow tubes made of the proteins alpha and beta tubulin that are part of a cell's cytoskeleton, a network of protein filaments that extends throughout the cell, gives the cell shape, and keeps its organelles in place. They are responsible for various kinds of movements in all eukaryotic cells. Microtubules are involved in nucleic and cell division, organization of intracellular structure, and intracellular transport, as well as ciliary and flagellar motility.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ribosomal RNA is actively synthesized in
questions.solution: The nucleolus is the largest, a round structure located inside the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell. It is a non-membranous structure, where biosynthesis of rRNA takes place. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is actively synthesized in the nucleolus. The nucleolus is also known as the ribosomal factory.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following are surface structures of a prokaryotic cell, but does not facilitate motility?
questions.solution: Besides flagella, pili and fimbriae are also surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein. The fimbriae are small bristle-like fibres sprouting out of the cell. In some bacteria, they attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The axoneme is found in
questions.solution: The electron microscopic study of a cilium or the flagellum shows that they are covered with the plasma membrane. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A protoplast is a cell:
questions.solution:
Plant cell - cell wall = Protoplast
Protoplast is a biological term proposed by Hanstein in 1880 to refer to the entire cell, excluding the cell wall, but currently has several definitions: a plant, bacterial or fungal cell that had its cell wall completely or partially removed using either mechanical or enzymatic means.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plasma membrane helps in
options: Transportation of only water in and out of cell
questions.solution: All cells are enclosed by a thin, film-like liable membrane called the plasma membrane or plasmalemma. The main function of the plasma membrane is to regulate the flow of materials into and out of the cell (osmoregulation). The membrane is selectively permeable.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Generally accepted features of the biological membrane include all of the following, except
options: Rapid diffusion of inorganic ions across lipid bilayer
It comprises of both intrinsic and extrinsic proteins
Lateral diffusion of integral and peripheral proteins
questions.solution: Polar substances because of charge cannot cross membrane easily. Only lipid-soluble substances can move across the membrane rapidly because of their hydrophobic nature. Special protein is needed to make ions to cross the membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following would you expect to find glyoxysomes?
questions.solution: Glyoxysomes are present in the fat-rich seed. It carries out a break down of fats into carbohydrates by glyoxylate cycle during seed germination to provide energy to the embryo. It also occurs in other fatty seeds like ground and mustard.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: All cells are enclosed by a thin, film-like liable membrane called the plasma membrane or plasmalemma. The main function of the plasma membrane is to regulate the flow of materials into and out of the cell (osmoregulation). The membrane is selectively permeable.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mycoplasmas, the smallest cells, are only (i) μm in length while bacteria could be (ii) μm. Among multicellular organisms, human red blood cells are about (iii)μm in diameter. Identify (i), (ii), and (iii).
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas, the smallest cells, are only 0.3 μm in length while bacteria could be 3 to 5 μm. Among multicellular organisms, human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cytoskeleton is made up of
questions.solution: The cytoskeleton is a system of proteinaceous fibrillar structures that pervades the cytoplasm. As such, it may be described as the part of the cytoplasm that provides the internal supporting framework for a cell. In addition to providing structural support, it's also involved in different types of movements (where it anchors various cellular structures like the flagellum) as well as the movement of cellular substances.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding mesosomes:

a. It may be present in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.
b. It helps in cell wall secretion, cell respiration, DNA replication and cell division
c. It increases the surface area of the cell wall and enzymatic content.
d. It contains oxidative enzymes.

Which of the above statements are true?
questions.solution: A special membranous structure called the mesosome is formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells. They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content. In some prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, there are other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called chromatophores which contain pigments.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The names of Schleiden and Schwann are associated with
options: Protoplasm as the physical basis of life
Nucleus functions as control centre of cell
questions.solution: Cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann (1839) according to which "All living organisms are composed of cells." Cell theory is also known as cell principle, cell doctrine etc.

Different cells have different sizes. Arrange the following cells in ascending order of their size and select the correct option.

Which of the following cellular organelles is/are bound by a single membrane?
Peroxisomes, Lysosomes, Mitochondria

Both peroxisomes and lysosomes but not mitochondria
questions.solution: The lysosomes are bound by a single unit membrane of 75 <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>A</mtext> <mo>∘</mo> </mover> </mrow> </math> . questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement with respect to centrioles.
options: They are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin.
The central part is non-proteinaceous and called the hub.
They form the basal body of cilia or flagella.
questions.solution: The central part of centriole is a proteinaceous structure called the hub.which is connected with peripheral triplets by radial spokes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately <u>           (i)           </u> protein and <u>         (ii)         </u> lipids.
questions.solution: The ratio of protein and lipids varies considerably in different cell types. In humans, the membrane of erythrocytes has approximately 52% protein and 40% lipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some of the enzymes, which are associated with the digestion of proteins, lipids and nucleic acids, are present in
questions.solution: The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases such as lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All the following statements regarding cell organelles are correct, except
options: Lysosomes are single-membrane vesicles budded off from Golgi apparatus and contain digestive enzymes
Endoplasmic reticulum consists of a network of membranous tubules and helps in transport, synthesis, and secretion
Leucoplasts are bound by a single membrane, lack pigment but contain their own DNA and protein-synthesizing machinery.
Sphaerosomes are single membrane-bound and are associated with synthesis and storage of lipids
questions.solution: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids which generally occur near the nucleus in non-green cells and possess internal lamellae. These double membranous structures are of three types: amyloplast, proteinoplast, and elaioplast. Amyloplasts can synthesize and store starch. Proteinoplasts store proteins but can not synthesize. Elaioplasts store lipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Antibiotics are usually not given for an ______  infection, as they may worsen the disease process.
questions.solution: E.coli is a prokaryote as it is a bacterium. Escherichia coli, is a type of bacteria that normally lives in the intestines. It’s also found in the gut of some animals. Most types of E. coli are harmless and even help keep your digestive tract healthy. But some strains can cause diarrhea if you eat contaminated food or drink fouled water. The treatment for the infection is to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration and to get as much rest as possible. Antibiotics are usually not given for this infection, as they may worsen the disease process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chemiosmotic theory of ATP synthesis in the chloroplasts and mitochondria is based on:
questions.solution: Chemiosmotic theory of ATP synthesis in the chloroplasts and mitochondria is based on proton gradient. Chemiosmosis is the movement of ions across a selectively permeable membrane, down their electrochemical gradient. More specifically, it relates to the generation of ATP by the movement of hydrogen ions across a membrane during cellular respiration or photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nucleolus usually associates with chromatin (or chromosomes) at a specific site called
questions.solution: Nucleolar organizer region present on chromosome helps in the reappearance of nucleolus after cell division. The number of NOR in a cell corresponds to the number of nucleoli present in the nucleus of the cell. In a human cell, NOR occurs on chromosomes 13,14,15, 21 and 22.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

A Thylakoids (i) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus
B Cristae (ii) Condensed structure of DNA
C Cisternae (iii) Flat membranous sacs in stroma
D Chromatin (iv) Infoldings in mitochondria
questions.solution: Thylakoids - Flat membranous sacs in the stroma of the chloroplast. Cristae - Infoldings in mitochondria. Cisternae - Disc-shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus. Chromatin - Condensed structure of DNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The endoplasmic reticulum is closely associated with the Golgi apparatus. Synthesized proteins from the RER are released from which part of the Golgi apparatus?
questions.solution: A number of proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a substitution of mitochondria in E. coli?
questions.solution: Mesosomes are unique membranous bacterial structures that actively function in cell injury and physiological cellular processes, such as replication and separation of nucleoids and oxidative phosphorylation. Mesosome is an enfolding of the bacterial cell membrane. It is rich in enzymes and increases surface area. It helps in respiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is proteinaceous and called the <u>          A             </u>, which is connected with tubules of the peripheral triplets by <u>            B             </u> made of protein.
questions.solution: The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is proteinaceous and called the hub, which is connected with tubules of the peripheral triplets by radial spokes made of protein. The centrioles form the basal body of cilia or flagella, and spindle fibres that give rise to the spindle apparatus during cell division in animal cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The vacuoles are surrounded by a thin membrane called
questions.solution: Large sap vacuoles are present in plants and they are surrounded by thin membrane called tonoplast, and the fluid present inside is called tonoplasm. Tonoplast facilitates the movement of ions against the concentration gradient from cytoplasm to cell sap.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select incorrect pairing.
options: Heterochromatin - Darkly stained region of chromosome
questions.solution:
Polytene chromosomes are oversized chromosomes that are developed from standard chromosomes. Specialized cells undergo repeated rounds of DNA replication without cell division (endomitosis), to increase cell volume, forming a giant polytene chromosome. They are present in the salivary glands of dipteran flies like Drosophila.

Lampbrush chromosomes are a special form of chromosomes that are found in the growing oocytes (immature eggs) of most animals, except mammals.

Lampbrush chromosomes are present in the amphibian oocytes/immature eggs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The structures that help some bacteria to attach to rocks and/or host tissue are
questions.solution: Fimbriae: Hollow tubular surface appendages, present in the bacterial cells, which help in an attachment to rocks and/or host tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organelles is bound by the tonoplast?
questions.solution: The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm. It contains water, sap, excretory product and other materials not useful for the cell. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane called tonoplast.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect one pair from the following.
questions.solution:
Protein synthesis takes place in ribosomes, which is attached to the surface of the endoplasmic reticulum by ribophorin-I and ribophorin-II.

Approximately 50 hydrolytic enzymes are found in the lysosome. They include proteases, nucleases, glycosidases, lipases, phospholipases, phosphatases and sulphatases. All lysosomal enzymes are acid hydrolases and optimally active at pH 5.0.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main function of lysosome is
questions.solution:
Lysosome was discovered by C de Duve.

The main functions of lysosomes are:

(i) Digestion of large extracellular particles

(ii) Digestion of intracellular substance

questions.subject: Botany

Match the column with respect to organelles and their respective function.
 
   Column I    Column II
 a.  Golgi apparatus  (i)  Helps in spindle formation
 b.  Ribosomes bound to ER  (ii)  Synthesis and storage of fats

The path of a protein destined for secretion has its origins in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, a membrane-bound compartment in the cell. MTOCs has two main functions: the organization of eukaryotic flagella and cilia and the organization of the mitotic and meiotic spindle apparatus, which separate the chromosomes during cell division. Spherosomes are small membrane-bound organelles which take part in storage and synthesis of fats.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the given organelle below, which part is associated with the packaging of materials to be delivered?
questions.solution: The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face. The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main organelle involved in modification and routing of newly synthesized proteins to their destinations is
questions.solution: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. A number of proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face. Golgi apparatus is the important site of the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of substances are found inside a mitochondrion?
questions.solution: The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Lysosomes, commonly called suicidal bags, consists of 40 different types of hydrolytic enzymes which are capable of digesting all biomolecules; thus, they carry out intracellular and extracellular digestion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

How many of the above statements are in common for mitochondria and chloroplast?
questions.solution: Mitochondria and chloroplast both have their own DNA and ribosomes, and are self-replicating. They both have a double membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following maintains continuity between the water and lipid phases inside and outside the cells?
questions.solution: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum produces nearly all of the lipids required for the elaboration of new cell membranes, including both phospholipids and cholesterol. The major phospholipid is made up of phosphatidylcholine, also called lecithin. Lecithin maintains continuity between the water and lipid phases inside and outside the cell.

Gas vacuoles are found in blue-green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.
