questions.q:
Which one of the following fits the below description?

It is a single-celled organism that is a greenish colour and has a cell wall around its cell membrane. It has small infoldings of the cell membrane. It contains genetic material in the cytoplasm which is devoid of any envelope. It has ribosomes for protein synthesis.
questions.solution: Since the DNA does not have any membranous covering, it is a prokaryotic cell. The small infoldings of the cell membrane are called mesosomes which are unique to prokaryotes. Thus, it will be a type of bacteria as all other options are eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following points were not explained by Schleiden and Schwann when they formulated their original cell theory?
options: All plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant
Animal cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the 'plasma membrane'
Cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells
The presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells
questions.solution: Many plants were observed by Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist. He observed that all plants are made up of different types of cells that combine to form different types of tissues. Theodore Schwann, a British zoologist, observed that various types of animal cells have a thin outer layer. It is called the plasma membrane today. He also concluded that the cell wall is a unique feature of plants. Later Rudolf Virchow added the concept of 'Omnis cellula-e cellula'. It means that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In cells actively participating in protein synthesis and secretion, which of the following organelles is frequently found?
questions.solution: The ER often shows ribosomes attached to their outer surface. The endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). In the absence of ribosomes, they appear smooth and are called the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER). RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. They are extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct order of sedimentation of subcellular structures during differential centrifugation is
questions.solution: Nucleus is the largest structure of cell which occupies upto 10% volume of the cell. Mitochondria is the largest cytoplasmic organelle in animal cell and ribosome is the smallest organelle of the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Radioactively-labelled d-nucleotides are introduced into a cell.



In which cell structures will the radioactivity first become concentrated?
questions.solution: Here, 2 and 3 are nucleus and mitochondria which contain DNA that made of nucleotide. Rest of the labelled organelles do not contain nucleotides/DNA where 1 is rough endoplasmic reticulum and 4 is golgi complex.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the given statements are incorrect?

I. Connectivity of plasmodesmata is maintained by ER membrane called dictyosome.
II. Totally buried proteins in membrane are integral protein while partially buried proteins are peripheral proteins.
III. The primary cell wall is capable of growth.
IV. The peroxisome is not included in the endomembrane system.
questions.solution: Connectivity of plasmodesmata is maintained by ER membrane called desmotubules. Both totally buried and partially buried proteins are called integral or intrinsic proteins and they cannot be easily separated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which type of cell contains the highest proportion of cell structures bound by a single membrane?
questions.solution: Goblet cell been secretory in function will have more amount of golgi bodies and vacuoles compared to other cells from the options.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Some features of cells are listed. Which features can be found both in plant cells and prokaryotic cells?

I. cell wall
II. cell surface membrane
III. ribosome
questions.solution: All the given feature are present in both plant cell and prokaryotic cell although the composition may vary. A plant cell has a cell wall (of cellulose), the cell membrane is present and also ribosome (80S) whereas prokaryotic cell mostly contains peptidoglycan as cell wall with 70S ribosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An electron micrograph of a plant cell shows two different types of plastids. One of them is known to store oils and fats in them; such a plastid is known as:
questions.solution: Based on the type of pigments plastids can be classified into chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts. The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Vesicles can be formed by which structures from the following?
 
  Cell Surface Membrane Endoplasmic Reticulum Golgi Body
I Yes Yes Yes
II Yes Yes No
III Yes No Yes
IV No Yes Yes
questions.solution: Vesicle is a structure within or outside a cell, consisting of liquid or cytoplasm enclosed by a membrane. All the three structure mentioned display formation of vesicles. Cell surface membrane helps in making food vacuoles, viz. amoeba endocytosis process where it ingest the food particles by making a vacuole which is a vesicle formed by the cell membrane. ER produces vesicles to enclose the products for movement within cell, viz. RER enclosed the protein in a vesicles and passes it to Golgi bodies for further processing. Lastly, golgi body has a characteristic feature of producing vesicles; viz., to release the secretion of a glandular cell out of the cell body that is exocytosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Analyze the following pairs and identify the correct option given.

I. Chromoplasts - Contain pigments other than chlorophyll
II. Leucoplasts - Devoid of any pigments
III. Amyloplasts - Store proteins
IV. Aleuroplasts - Store oils and fats
V. Elaioplasts - Store carbohydrates
questions.solution:
Plastids are mainly of two types:

(i) Coloured (including chromoplasts containing pigments other than chlorophyll and chloroplast containing green pigment chlorophyll).

(ii) Leucoplasts, which store reserve food material, these are devoid of any pigment and may be carbohydrate storing amyloplast, lipid storing elaioplast or protein storing proteinoplast (aleuroplast).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is true about ribosomes?
options: The prokaryotic ribosomes are 80S, where "S" stands for sedimentation coefficient
These are composed of ribonucleic acid and proteins
These are found only in eukaryotic cells
These are self-splicing introns of some RNAs.
questions.solution: Ribosomes are non-membranous (i.e., without membrane) cell organelles composed of rRNA and protein. These are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. In prokaryotes, ribosomes are 70s type, whereas in eukaryotes, they are 80S type.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The walls of sieve tubes develop into sieve plates together getting associated with _________.
questions.solution: The plasmodesmata act as channels between the cell walls of adjacent plant cells. They are mainly involved in transport and cell to cell recognition. Structurally, the sieve tubes wall is dispersed with plasmodesmata and are grouped together. Later, these areas of the tube walls and plasmodesmata develop into sieve plates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Some secretory cells synthesize and release glycoproteins. What is the correct order of the sequence of events as they occur in the secretory cell?

I. Exocytosis

II. Product accumulates in secretory vesicle

III. mRNA binds to ribosomes

IV. Synthesis of glycoprotein
questions.solution: Protein synthesis follows the typical transcription to translation steps. The mRNA having the code for glycoprotein will be translated by the ribosome possibly in the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). Later the constructed protein is processed by golgi bodies and secreted out of the cell via exocytosis in vesicles made out of the golgi bodies. Such secretory cells have a higher amount of RER and GB.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a prokaryotic cell, mesosomes functions is
options: DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells.

Formation of cell wall, increase the surface area of
the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.
questions.solution: A special membranous structure is a mesosome that is formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells. They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the row having features true for a typical plant cell.
 
  Cell Wall Ribosome Cell Diameter
I Cellulose 80S 1-5μm
II Cellulose 70S and 80S 10-100μm
III Peptidoglycan 70S 1-5μm
IV Peptidoglycan 70S and 80S 5-40μm
questions.solution: A typical plant cell is a eukaryotic cell having its cell wall made of primarily cellulose and cell size range is larger than prokaryote (0.5–1μm) approximately 10–100μm. A plant cell has an 80S type ribosome present in the cytoplasm and its chloroplast has 70S ribosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The figure below represents the structure of the chromosome.



Select the correct option regarding the structure.
options: 1 - Centromere, 2 - Chromatid, and the number of chromosome is 1
1 - Centromere, 2 - Telomere,  and the number of chromosome is 2
1 - Chromatid, 2 - Telomere, and the number of chromosome is 1
1 - Telomere, 2 - Chromatid and the number of chromosome is 2
questions.solution:
Centromere is the primary constriction found in chromosome of dividing cells. Centromere holds the two sister chromatids together. Each chromatid generally have 2 DNA; thus, a chromosome of 2 sister chromatids will have 4 DNA.

Telomere is the end or the terminal region of a chromosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The chromosomes can be divided based on the position of the centromere. A certain chromosome appears 'L' shaped during the anaphase stage and has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome. Such a chromosome will be
questions.solution: The metacentric chromosome has a middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting in one shorter arm and one long arm. In case of an acrocentric chromosome, the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following does not differ in E. coli and Chlamydomonas?
questions.solution: Although E. coli is a prokaryotic cell with a peptidoglycan cell wall and Chlamydomonas is eukaryotic with a cellulosic cell wall, but they have cell membrane as a common structure which is essentially the same and is made up of phospholipid bilayer. Other components as mentioned above namely- ribosomes, cell wall & nuclear organization differ in these organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The passage through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions is
questions.solution: Material can move in and out of the nucleus through nuclear pore. Especially, the RNA molecule is synthesized in the nucleolus and for protein synthesis in the cytoplasm they come out through the nuclear pore of the nucleus. The synthesized protein moves to the nucleus to perform replication, transcription etc. Plasmodesmata are the small pores in plant where the movement of all the molecules takes place, they are the place for communication between plant cells. Kinetochores are proteinaceous structure present at the side of the centromere for the attachment of spindle fibre during cell division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Microfilaments are involved in
questions.solution: Microfilaments are involved in the process of celldivision by the formation of cleavage furrow in animal cells. The cell streaming or amoeboid movement is mediated by these cytoskeletal elements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
(i) Mitochondria and chloroplast possess small and circular non-histone DNA.

(ii) Mesosomes are extension of plasma membrane.

(iii) Quasi fluid nature of lipid enables flip flop movement of proteins at a specific place.

(iv) Components of endomembrane system associated with secretion, packaging of material and capable of digestion of several macro organic compounds.

From given, incorrect statement is/are
questions.solution: The quasi fluid nature of the lipid helps in the lateral movement of protein through the membrane bilayer. The protein can move through the membrane and not only at specific places. Mitochondria and plastid are semi-autonomous organelle as they have DNA similar to bacteria and partially depend on nucleus. Endomembrane system comprises of ER, Golgi, vacuole, lysosome, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: ________ concluded that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.
questions.solution: It was observed by Schleiden that all tissues of the plants are composed of different kinds of cells. The different kinds of animal and plant cells were studied by Schwann. He observed that animal cells had a thin outer layer which later was named as plasma membrane. Through his observations on the plant tissues he also concluded that an unique  character found in the plant cells is the presence of cell wall. The cell theory was together formulated by Schleiden and Schwann. Rudolf Virchow was the first person to explain that new cells arise from cell division of pre-existing cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following organelle in the figure CORRECTLY matches with its functions?
options: Rough endoplasmic reticulum, formation of lipids
questions.solution: Endoplasmic reticulum is a network of tubular structures present in the cytoplasm which divide the intracellular space into luminal and extra luminal. These ER can be divided into two types depending upon the presence of ribosome on their outer surface. The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has ribosomes on the outer surface while the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks presence of ribosomes. RER is involved in protein synthesis and secretion where as SER is involved in synthesis of lipids and lipid like hormones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The ribosomes present in the cytoplasm of the causative organism of cholera and mitochondria of causative organism of malaria, respectively, are
questions.solution: Causative organism of cholera is a bacterium Vibrio cholerae. It is a prokaryote. The causative organism of malaria is Plasmodium which is a protozoan. It is a eukaryote. Ribosomes are the granular structures composed of RNA and proteins. They are not surrounded by any membrane and are seen as dense particles under the electron microscope. Ribosomes found in cytoplasm of eukaryotic organisms are 80S and those in cytoplasm of prokaryotic organisms are 70S, where S is the coefficient of sedimentation and is a measure of the density and size of the ribosome. Mitochondria of eukaryotes also have ribosome which resemble prokaryotes. They are 70S.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The 'Fluid Mosaic Model' of plasma membrane was proposed by
questions.solution: In Eukaryotes the cell membrane is explained as Fluid Mosaic Model by Schleiden and Schwann. According to this model the plasma membrane is made up of Lipids and Proteins. The lipids are arranged in a bilayer. The lipids present are phospholipids. These are arranged in such a way that the polar heads are towards the outer side and hydrophobic ends are towards the inner side. The ratio of proteins and lipids are different in different cell types. In humans it is seen that around 40 percent is lipid and 52 percent is protein. This was explained as Fluid Mosaic model. This explains that the quasi- fluid nature of lipid causes the movement of proteins throughout the bilayer structure. This is termed as fluidity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A gram <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> bacteria differs from a Gram <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> bacteria because of
questions.solution: Bacteria can be classified into two groups on the basis of the differences in the cell envelopes and the manner in which they respond to the staining procedure developed by Christian Gram. Those that takes up the gram stain are called gram positive and the other that do not takes up gram stain are called gram negative bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In eukaryotic cells, the proteins that will function as ribonucleoproteins are made by
questions.solution: Ribosomes are made up of ribonucleoproteins, rRNA and proteins. Nucleolus is called ribosome factory of cell. Thus synthesis of ribonucleoprotein which makes ribosomes occurs in nucleolus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the option having all correct statements.

a ER divide the intercellular space into two distinct compartments.

b The cis and the trans face of the Golgi body are entirely different but interconnected.

c Lysosomes are the single membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi body.

d In plant cells, the vacuole can occupy up to 90 percent of the volume of the cell.
questions.solution: ER divide the intercellular space into two distinct compartments, luminal chamber and extra luminal chamber. Cis and trans face of golgi body are entirely different but interconnected. Lysosomes are formed by golgi body. Vacuole in a plant cell can occupy upto 90 % volume.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following features is incorrectly described for prokaryotic cell in comparison to a eukaryotic cell?
options:
Feature Description
Cell size smaller

Feature Description
Ribosomes 70s, instead of 80s
questions.solution:
Features Prokaryotic cells Eukaryotic cells
1. Size Small sized Moderate to large sized
2. Cell wall Usually present Present/absent
3. Multiplication Rapid Generally not rapid
4. Nucleus Genetic material is not membrane bound and is termed as nucleoid or incipient nucleus or genophore Well defined membrane bound nucleus is present in which genetic material is present in the form of chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The cytoskeletal elements are involved in:

(i) Amoeboid movement
(ii) Separation of chromosomes
(iii) Ciliary movement
(iv) Formation of cell plate
questions.solution:
Cell movement; is both internal, referred to as cytoplasmic streaming, and external, referred to as motility. Internal movements of organelles are governed by actin filaments and other components of the cytoskeleton. These filaments make an area in which organelles such as chloroplasts can move. Internal movement is known as cytoplasmic streaming. External movement of cells is determined by special organelles for locomotion. These could be pseudopodia, cilia and flagella.

The cytoskeletal elements are required for the delivery of vesicles to the equatorial region of the cell and provide guidance to the cell plate. Vesicles, originating from the Golgi apparatus, travel along microtubules and fuse in a unique manner at the center of the phragmoplast to give rise to the new plasma membranes of the two daughter cells. The cargo they carry contributes to the cell-plate matrix.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Protein synthesis in an animal cell occurs
options: Only on the ribosomes present in cytosol
Only on ribosomes attached to the nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum
On ribosomes present in the nucleolus as well as in cytoplasm
On ribosomes present in cytoplasm as well as in mitochondria
questions.solution: Protein synthesis in a animal cell occurs on ribosomes present in cytoplasm as well as in mitcohondria because mitochondrie and chloroplast also have their own DNA, RNA and ribosome so can synthesize half of their required proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cell organelle showing extensive polymorphism is
questions.solution: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles. These are formed by the Golgi apparatus and contain many hydrolytic enzymes. These enzymes become active in acidic pH and bring about the process of phagocytosis and hence are regarded as suicidal bags. Thus, by forming pseudopodia they also show extensive polymorphism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many cell organelles are bounded by a single membrane?
Nucleolus, ER, Sphaerosome, Ribosomes, Mitochondria, Lysosome, Peroxisome, Golgi body, Nucleus.
questions.solution: Lysosome, peroxisome, golgi body, ER, and sphaerosomes are bounded by single membrane. Mitochondria and Nucleus are bounded by double membrane. Nucleolus and ribosomes are membraneless organelle, not bounded by any membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ion carriers are located in
questions.solution: The surface of the plasma membrane has the ion carriers which participate in the exchange of ions. The surface layer of the plasma membrane is composed of surface proteins or integral protein channels like ion channels.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cell organelle of the eukaryotic cell shows fission?
questions.solution: Plastid divides by fission to form pro plastid which further develops to form different type of plastid required by the cell. Mitochondria and plastid are similar and both divides by fission to increase their number.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A large number of proteins made by the ribosomes get modified in
questions.solution: Camillo Golgi first explained Golgi apparatus. These are of various shape like flat, disc shaped sacs or cisternae. The golgi bodies are arranged with covex cis which is the forming face and concave trans which is the maturing face. The cis and trans are interconnected with each other. Large number of proteins made by the ribosomes get modified in Cisternae of golgi apparatus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If cells are broken up and sedimented by centrifugation, the new structures formed in one of the fractions is
questions.solution: When cells are broken up under laboratory conditions, the endoplasmic reticulum breaks out to form microsomes. These are small bodies that are absent in healthy, living cells and these structures are important for many experimental purposes. Being similar to ER these structures are used to perform protein synthesis on a membrane and this helps to understand the actual process that occurs in the cell, as these microsomes mimic the activity of the endoplasmic reticulum in a test tube.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Both centrioles in a centrosome lie ..........(i)........ to each other and each of them contains ....(ii)..... peripheral fibril so ........(iii)......... array is present.
questions.solution: Centrosome consists of two centrioles which lies perpendicular to each other and a pair of centriole is called as diplosome. Each centriole consists of nine peripheral fibril and a central protein hub. It thus shows  <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>  arrangement.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the wrong statements.

(i) All eukaryotic cells are identical.

(ii) All eukaryotic cells show compartmentalization.

(iii) Centrioles are absent in almost all plant cells.

(iv) Animal cells contain no large central vacuoles.
questions.solution: All eukaryotic cells are not identical because plant cells have cell wall, large central vacuole and generally no centriole while animal cells have no cell wall, no central vacuole and centrioles present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In human beings, the plasma membrane of the erythrocytes has approximately ____ protein and ____ lipids
questions.solution: The initial studies carried out about the cell membrane, before the advent of electron microscope, had showed that the plasma membrane in erythrocytes is composed of lipids arranged in a bilayer with the polar heads on the outer side and hydrophilic heads on the inner. Lipid component mainly consisted of phosphoglycerides. Later through biochemical investigations it was found that human erythrocytes have around 40 % lipids and 52% proteins in the plasma membrane. The proteins can be divided into two types - integral and peripheral, depending on how easily they can be extracted.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Glycolipids in the plasma membrane are located at
options: Inner leaflet of the plasma membrane
The outer leaflet of the plasma membrane
Evenly distributed in the inner and outer leaflets
It varies according to cell types
questions.solution: In eukaryotes, the cell membrane is explained as a fluid mosaic model by Schleiden and Schwann. According to this model the plasma membrane is made up of lipids and proteins. The lipids are arranged in a bilayer. The lipids present are phospholipids. These are arranged in such a way that the polar heads are towards the outer side and hydrophobic ends are towards the inner side. The ratio of proteins and lipids are different in different cell types. In humans it is seen that around 40 percent is lipid and 52 percent is protein. This explains that the quasi- fluid nature of lipid causes the movement of proteins throughout the bilayer structure. The glycolipids are oriented towards outside the plasma membrane and are extrinsic in nature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The mineral present in cell wall is
questions.solution:
Cell wall is the outermost covering in the plant cell. The cell wall provides support to the cell. It is made up of
  • Matrix: Water (60%), hemicellulose (5-15%), pectic substances (2-8%), lipids (0.5-3%), proteins (1-2%).
  • Microfibrils: Cellulose (10-15%).
  • Other ingredients: Lignin, cutin, suberin, silica, minerals-calcium, iron and carbonate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Axoneme having <math><mn>9</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>2</mn></math> doublet microtubule arrangement is found in
questions.solution: Cilia and flagella are extensions that arise from the cell membrane. Flagella are longer than cilia. Both structures are responsible for cell motility. The microscopic features of these two structures are also very similar. The central core is known as axoneme. These show nine pairs of microtubules that are arranged peripherally and one pair of microtubule is also seen in the centre. This is <math><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> arrangement. The central tubules are connected to some peripheral tubules by means of a sheath.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Elaioplasts store
questions.solution: Plastids are found in plant cells. These consist of pigments. Based on the type of pigments, these are further classified as chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which brings about photosynthesis. Chromoplasts contain colored pigments like carotenes, xanthophylls, etc. This is responsible for the colored part of the plant. Leucoplasts are colorless plastids and contain stored nutrients. These can be amyloplasts if they store carbohydrates. This is seen in potatoes etc. elaioplasts store oils, fats and aleuroplasts contain proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which cell organelle comprises of cis and trans faces?
questions.solution: Golgi body are the only organelle which shows polarity. Cisternae are disc like parallely placed structure which gets curved. Curvature results in formation of concave and convex face. Convex face is known as cis or forming face which always lies towards nucleus and concave or trans or maturing face which always lies towards cell membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In mitochondria, cristae act as sites for
questions.solution: Mitochondria are power house of the cell. It consists of two membranes. Outer and inner. Outer membrane is smooth but inner membrane shows presence of many infoldings known as cristae. These increase the surface area of the membrane. These act as site for oxidation reduction reaction. Chemiosmosis and Electron transport chain takes place on the inner membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Middle lamella is
options: plasma membrane covering the two cells together.
made of calcium pectate or magnesium pectate.
a pore in the plasma membrane of cell.
a cell wall between two adjacent cells.
questions.solution: Cell wall is the outermost layer in the eukaryotic cells (absent in animals). It is a non -living and rigid layer. The main function is to protect the cells and also to give shape to the cells. It also prevents entry of unimportant substances. Young cells contain three layers: Primary wall, middle lamella and Secondary wall. Primary wall is responsible for growth and hence it is not seen in adult cells. Middle lamella is seen in all types of cells. This contains calcium pectate which helps to stick to the neighbouring cells. Plasmodesmata connects the middle lamella and cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The lysosome contains hydrolytic enzymes. For the functioning of enzymes, the pH inside the lysosome is
options: independent of the H+ ion concentration.
decreased by active pumping of H+ to the cytoplasm.
increased by simple diffusion of H+ from the cytoplasm.
dependent on the K+ ion concentration of the cytoplasm.
questions.solution: Lysosomes are formed by budding off vesicles from the Golgi apparatus. They are bounded by a single membrane about 500 nm and are involved in intracellular digestion, containing the enzymes needed to digest all types of macromolecules. The enzymes present in such vesicles belong to acid hydrolases: The acidic condition is maintained by pumping protons into the interior of the lysosomes from the cytoplasm. (Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that require acidic pH to function, for the functioning of these enzymes pH is decreased by actively pumping H+ to the cytoplasm).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Golgi apparatus is derived from
questions.solution: Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus and organelles. These include cell membrane, cell wall (absent in animal cells), nucleus, endomembrane system, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi apparatus, lysosomes, plastids, ribosomes, cytoskeleton, microtubules etc. Golgi apparatus is named after his discoverer Camillo Golgi. These consist of many sacs or cisternae arranged parallelly to each other. The main function of Golgi is to pack the proteins which are formed in the endoplasmic reticulum. Golgi apparatus consists of two sides: the concave or cis or forming face and the convex or trans or maturing face. The forming face will collect the unpacked materials from ER and the pack it and it is released from the convex side. The Golgi is able to receive it from ER because it is derived from it.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following filamentous structures are a structural component of the centriole?
questions.solution: Cytoplasm consists of different proteinaceous filamentous and tubular structure which are called as cyto skeleton, it includes microtubules and microfilaments. Microtubules are structural component of centriole and flagella.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which cell organelle is absent in the leaves of onion?
questions.solution:
There are many differences between animal and plant cells. These are as follows;

ANIMAL CELL PLANT CELL
1. Cell wall is absent Cell wall is seen outside the cell membrane
2. Vacuoles are small and numerous Vacuoles are large and normally single
3. Centrioles are present Centrioles are absent
4. Nucleus is in the centre Nucleus to one side.
5. Chloroplasts are absent Chloroplasts are present


Onion being a plant cell lacks centrioles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following subcellular structures cannot be isolated?
questions.solution: When cells are broken up in the lab microsomes are formed. These are similar in activity to Endoplasmic reticulum. These structures are important and used for many experimental purposes. Being similar to ER these structures are used to perform Protein synthesis on a membrane and this helps to understand the actual process that occurs in the cell. Hence ER is always obtained in the form of microsomes and thus cannot be isolated completely. However other organelles can be isolated in the form.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nucleolus is:
options: Rounded structure found in cytoplasm near nucleus
Rounded structure inside nucleus and having <math><mi>r</mi></math>RNA
Rod-shaped structure in cytoplasm near the nucleus
questions.solution:
Nucleolus is a rounded structure present inside nucleus, having rRNA.

First observed by Fontana in the skin cells of eel. Term nucleolus was coined by Bowman. Microscopic structure was given by Wagner.

It is associated with nucleolar organizer region of the nucleolar chromosome.
No covering membrane around nucleolus. Nucleolus has four components-amorphous matrix, granular portion, fibrillar portion and chromatin portion, Nucleolus consists of homogeneous matrix called pars amorpha. it contains scattered granules and fibrils Generally, two nucleoli are present in each cell but number may vary.

∙  Functions :

⋆  It is store house of RNA.

⋆  It produces and stores ribosomal RNA.

⋆  It forms the units of ribosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the statements given below with regard to the functions performed by the Golgi apparatus.

I. Transport and chemically modify the material contained within it.
II. Secrete mucin in the respiratory tract.
III. Secrete slime in the insectivorous plants.

Which of the following is the CORRECT answer?
options: I is wrong but II and III are correct
II is wrong but I and III are correct
II and III are wrong but I is correct
I, II and III are correct
questions.solution: Golgi apparatus is a membrane-bound organelle of eukaryotic present in cytoplasm and composed of flattened, stacked pouches called cisternae. It is responsible for transporting, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids into vesicles for delivery to targeted destinations. Many types of cells contain only one or several Golgi apparatus, plant cells can contain hundreds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The mitochondria
questions.solution: Mitochondria are power houses of the cells. These divide by binary fission. Fission takes place with DNA replication. Proteins are needed for this process. These are semiautonomous organelles as they have their own DNA and thus can coordinate its division too.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The special arrangement of lipids in the cell membrane ensures that the
options: polar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
non-polar tail of unsaturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
polar tail of unsaturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
non-polar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
questions.solution: The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent of the electron microscope in the 1950s. Meanwhile, chemical studies on the cell membrane, especially in human red blood cells (RBCs), enabled the scientists to deduce the possible structure of plasma membrane. These studies showed that the cell membrane is composed of lipids that are arranged in a bilayer. Also, the lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards the inner part.This ensures that the nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment. The lipid component of the membrane mainly consists of phosphoglycerides.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The theory given by Schleiden and Schwann and modified by Virchow is not applicable to:
questions.solution: Schleiden and Schwann proposed a cell theory. He said that cells are the basic unit of life and all plants and animals are composed of the cells. In 1855, Rudolf Virchow added the third principle to cell theory. He states that Omnis e cellula e cellula means that all living cells come from pre-existing cells. Virchow's theory not applied to the virus because viruses are obligate parasites which means they cannot complete its life cycle without a host. They do not have cellular machinery whereas in others it is present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is called the fret membrane?
questions.solution: This membrane is found in the chloroplast. This organelle is present within plants and algae to carry out photosynthesis. They have a double-layered membrane that encloses a matrix called the stroma. In the stroma, a membrane-bound structure is present i.e .thylakoid which arranges as a stack to form granum. Grana connects to each other through stroma lamellae. It is also known as intergranal lamellae or fret lamellae. Space which is present in stroma lamellae is called fret channels and they have enzymes for carbon dioxide fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organelles is present exclusively in plants?
questions.solution: The glyoxysome was discovered by Beevers and Breidenbach in 1961. These are specialized peroxisomes that are found only in plants(germinating seeds). They also possess the key enzyme for the glyoxylate cycle. They contain an enzyme that initiates the breakdown of fatty acids and also helps in the synthesis of sugar by gluconeogenesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
I. ER is also called the control center of the cell.

II. It modifies chemicals that are toxic to the cell.

III. SER is a major site for the synthesis of proteins.

IV. ER is a network of interconnected cisternae, tubules, and vesicles present in the endoplasm.

Which of the following statement is/are not true about the ER.
questions.solution: ER is a single membrane-bounded structure that forms a channel-like structure in the cytoplasm. It consists of the empty lumen, luminal chamber, inside ER and extraluminal chamber, outside ER. SER carries out lipid synthesis and detoxification of toxic chemicals. It is a network of interconnected cisternae, tubules, and vesicles present in the endoplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding mitochondria?
options: The matrix possesses a single double-stranded circular DNA molecule.
It is the site of anaerobic respiration.
The outer membrane is continuous and smooth.
Mitochondria multiply by a fission-like division.
questions.solution: Mitochondria is the site for aerobic respiration. It is surrounded by two membranes, the outer membrane which is smooth, and the inner membrane which is folded into finger-like projections called cristae. Mitochondria divide by fission to increases its number.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct match.
questions.solution: Food can be stored in the form of carbohydrates in amyloplast, aleuroplast stores proteins, and elaioplast stores lipids. Pyrenoids are special structures present in the chloroplast of algae which stores starch. Tubers are stem modification for the storage of carbohydrates and liver is an organ that stores glycogen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct for the vacuoles?
options: Contractile vacuoles are helpful in excretion
Usually tonoplast facilitates the transport of ions against the concentration gradient into the cytoplasm
Food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles
Sap vacuole is bound by a single membrane
questions.solution: The three major components of the tonoplast are two proton pumps, the vacuolar H<sup>+</sup>-ATPase facilitates transportation in the vacuole.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct option of organelle with its function.
options: Golgi apparatus - packaging and transportation of proteins
Lysosomes - excretion in some organisms like Amoeba
RER - synthesis and breakdown of lipids
Cilia - hair-like appendage which plays a role in bacterial conjugation
questions.solution: Golgi body are main site for processing, packaging and transportation of proteins. RER transfers its newly synthesized protein on cis face of golgi body and mature proteins are released on trans face. Lysosome carries out intracellular and extracellular digestion, RER is site of protein synthesis. Cell membrane is selectively permeable.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Integral proteins are present on the surface of the membrane.
Phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer, which is the major constituent of the cell membrane.
The cell membrane of RBCs consists of 40% lipids and 52% proteins.
questions.solution: The cell membrane consists of two types of proteins: integral proteins are intrinsic proteins which are present deeply embedded in the lipid bilayer and cannot be easily removed, external proteins are present on the surface and loosely associated with the lipid bilayer.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The set of the organelles/structure that are absent in plant cell are
questions.solution: Centriole is membrane less structure present in animal cell and some lower plant cell. It is absent in all higher plant cell. Centriole helps in formation of spindle fibre during cell division. It forms basal granule or belpharoplast which form cilia and flagella.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ribososomes are CORRECTLY characterized by which of the following statements?
options: They are composed entirely of r-RNA
They are composed of two equal subunits.
They differ in response to antibiotics depending on whether they are eukaryotic or prokaryotic in origin.
They are composed of three equal subunits.
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are membrane less organelles found in both types of cells- eukaryote and prokaryote. Ribosomes are made of mix of proteins and ribosomal RNA. This organelle is important for the process of protein synthesis. It helps in translating mRNA and joining the amino acids together forming long polypeptide chain. Each ribosome is made up of two subnits - one large subunit and other small subunits.

The ribosomes of the eukaryotes are of 80S type and that of prokaryotes are of 70S.

Antibiotics are chemicals that kill or inhibit growths of bacterial cells. Certain antibiotics work by targeting the ribosomes where it inhibits the ribosomal functions either by blocking peptide formation or interfering with the translation process. Antibiotics chemical bind to the ribosomal subunits and inhibit the process. The bacterial antibiotics are specific to the prokaryotic ribosome and do not bind to the eukaryotic ribosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The vacuole in the plant cell contains
questions.solution: Plant cell is a eukaryotic type cell with well defined nucleus. It has a cell wall and chloroplast (for phosynthesis). The plant cell contains a large organelle, vacuole. It contains water, cell sap, excretory products and other substances. The vacuole is enclosed by a single membrane called tonoplast. The membrane facilitates movement of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradient.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All of the following processes occur in the endomembrane system, except
questions.solution:
The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system.

Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins. 

The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.

Protein synthesis and its modification process are carried out by the organelles of endoplasmic system. Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

In Amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organelles does not have a double layer?
questions.solution: Eukaryotic cell have many organelleles. These include Nucleus, Endomembrane System, Chloroplasts, Mitochondria, Peroxisomes. Endomembrane system is formed by Lysosomes, Vacuoles, Golgi apparatus and Endoplasmic reticulum as their functions are coordinated. Lysosomes are single membrane bound structures. These are formed by Golgi apparatus. These contain enzymes which bring about digestion of substances. These are regarded as suicidal bags. But Nuclei, Chloroplasts and Mitochondria are double membrane structures. In nuclei the outer and inner membrane encloses a perinuclear space. In Mitochodria the inner membrane forms cristae that are infoldings whereas outer membrane is smooth. Chloroplasts too shows outer and inner distinct layers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which set of the cell organelles are considered to be semi-autonomous?
questions.solution: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous as they posseses single circular double stranded DNA, by which they can synthesized RNA and uses ribosomes to synthesized some proteins required by them, thus called as semi autonomous organelle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A type of cell called a lymphocyte makes proteins that are exported from the cell. It is possible to track the path of these proteins within the cell by labeling them with radioactive isotopes. Which of the following might be the path of the protein from the site where its polypeptides are made to the lymphocyte's plasma membrane?
options: Nucleus  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  Golgi body  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  RER  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  Plasma membrane
questions.solution: The surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with the ribosome. It is located near the nucleus and continues with the outer layer of the nuclear envelope. This RER is very important in the synthesis and packaging of proteins. These proteins are transported through tubules to the smooth endoplasmic reticulum that lies near to the Golgi apparatus and then these proteins diffuse to the deepest layer of the Golgi apparatus with the help of transport vehicles. Then these proteins are transported to the cell membrane or plasma membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The nucleolus is an important site for
questions.solution: The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane-bound structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis. Larger and more numerous nucleoli are present in cells actively carrying out protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement about the plasma membrane.
options: The bilipid layer is made up of phosphoglycerides.
The membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately 40 per cent protein and 52 per cent lipids.
Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of membrane while the integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.
The fluid nature of the membrane is important for functions like cell growth and formation of intercellular junctions.
questions.solution:
The lipid component of the membrane mainly consists of phosphoglycerides.
The ratio of protein and lipid varies considerably in different cell types. In human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.
Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of membrane while the integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.
The fluid mosaic model was introduced by Singer and Nicholson. The fluid nature of the membrane is important for functions like cell growth and formation of intercellular junctions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Cytoskeleton provides mechanical support to the cell
Cytoskeleton helps in motility and maintenance of shape of cell
Cytoskeleton also occurs in prokaryotic cell.
questions.solution: Cytoskeleton are small proteinaceous filament-like structure that is randomly scattered in the cytoplasm. It includes microtubules and microfilaments, which provides mechanical support to the cell and helps in motility. Cytoskeleton are completely absent in a prokaryotic cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not present in the stroma of chloroplast?
questions.solution: The stroma of chloroplast consists of double-stranded DNA, ribosomes of 70S type (smaller than cytoplasmic ribosomes which are 80S) and all enzymes for the dark reaction or Calvin cycle of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct pairing.
options: ER - Formation of new nuclear membrane
questions.solution: Amyloplast is the site of storage of carbohydrates. The centrosome is responsible for the organization, and nucleation of microtubules while lysosome contains a digestive enzyme that is used to destroy invading viruses and bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mesosome helps in all the following processes except:
questions.solution: A special membranous structure is a mesosome which is formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells. They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The basic structure of the cell membrane
options: is a lipid bilayer that serves as a barrier to water-soluble molecules.
is a lipid bilayer that serves as a barrier to lipid-soluble molecules.
is best described as lipids dispersed within a protein bilayer.
​is a protein bilayer that serves as a barrier to lipid-soluble molecules.
questions.solution: Plasma membrane or the cell membrane separates the inside environment of cell from the outside environment. It protects the cell from the exterior environment. The cell membrane is mainly made of proteins and phospholipids. The phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer pattern with the hydrophobic tail on the inside and the hydrophilic head towards the outside. This protects the tail from aqueous environment and serves as a barrier to water-soluble molecule. The proteins are found on the surface of the membrane and also embedded within the membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cell organelle that is in close proximity to the cis face of Golgi bodies is
questions.solution:
A dense network of tubular structures distributed in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cell is called as endoplasmic reticulum. It is part of the endomembrane system of the cell. The organelles involved in the synthesis of protein, lipids and steroids.

The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes is:
questions.solution: These are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: RNA is absent in:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Plasmalemma is a plasma membrane that is present in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. They act as a barrier between the outer and inner surface of a cell. The plasmalemma encloses the contents of the cell and separates it from the outer environment. It is composed of lipids and proteins and they do not possess RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Polysome is formed by
options: several ribosomes attached to a single mRNA.
ribosomes attached to each other in a linear arrangement.
many ribosomes attached to a strand of endoplasmic reticulum
questions.solution: It is a cluster of numerous ribosomes that are involved in protein synthesis. These ribosomes in a polysome are connected with single mRNA and translate the genetic information coded in the mRNA. Each ribosome has two subunits i.e.one smaller and one bigger unit. Once the translation is finished these subunits get separated from each other. In the next cycle, they again reassociate for the initiation of protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell wall shows
questions.solution: The cell wall was first observed and named by Robert Hooke in 1665. It is a structural layer that surrounds some types of cells and situated outside the cell membrane. They provide cell structural support and protection. The cell wall in prokaryotes is made up of peptidoglycan and in eukaryotes, it is made up of polysaccharide and cellulose. The cell wall is completely permeable to water, molecules, and proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Find out the incorrect statements:

A. PPLO is a prokaryotic cell.
B. W.B.C. shows amoeboid movement.
C. Mesosomes helps in the synthesis of carbohydrates.
D. Microbodies are cell organelles.
E. Prokaryotes have endomembrane cell-organelles.
questions.solution:
A special membranous structure is a mesosome which is formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells. They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content. 

No organelles, like the ones in eukaryotes, are found in prokaryotic cells except for ribosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ribosomes are classified according to their
questions.solution: The ribosome is a large complex molecule that is found in prokaryote and eukaryote. They serve as the primary site for protein synthesis. In prokaryote, it is found in the free form in cytoplasm and in a eukaryote, it is found attached to the outer membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum. The ribosome is made up of two subunits i.e. large and small subunits. They are classified according to their sedimentation rate. Based on the sedimentation value they can be classified into the 70S and 80S ribosomes. 80S ribosome is found in the cytoplasm and the 70S ribosome is found in mitochondria and chloroplast.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One important component of cytoskeleton is
questions.solution: Eukaryotic cells are composed of a network of fibrous proteins that are called cytoskeleton and it is present in the cytoplasm. The cytoskeletal filaments are microfilaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments and they help in maintaining the shape of the cell. It is a dynamic structure because microtubules and microfilaments can depolymerize and repolymerize easily.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tonoplast is a
questions.solution: Large sap vacuole is present in plant cells and is surrounded by a membrane called tonoplast and the fluid present inside is called tonoplasm. Tonoplast facilitates the movement of ions against the concentration gradient from the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is incorrect in relation to the difference between plant and animal cell?
options:
Character Animal Cell Plant Cell
Cell wall Absent Present

Character Animal Cell Plant Cell
Cell division Division is anastral Division is astral

Character Animal Cell Plant Cell
Reserve food Glycogen Starch
questions.solution: Cell division in an animal cell is astral as they have centriole and astral rays develop from them. In plant cell, astral rays are absent thus their division is anastral.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: New cell arises from
questions.solution: Rudolf Virchow first stated that 'Omnis cellulae e cellulae' which means that all cell arises from the pre-existing cell by division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is closest to the plasma membrane?
questions.solution:
Vacuoles are membrane bound storage organelles found in plant cells and animal cells. They are in larger size in plants compared to animal cells. The membrane of vacuole is called as tonoplast.

The cell wall found around the cells of plants contain multiple layers. The outermost thin, flexible and extensible layer is the primary cell wall layer of the plant. The thick layer sandwiched between the plasmalemma and primary cell wall is the secondary cell wall. The middle lamella connects the adjacent cell walls of the cells and is rich in pectin. It also forms the plasmodesmata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a plastid?
questions.solution: Plastids are membrane bound organelles found in cells of plants, algae and some other organisms from eukaryotic group. These organelles are involved in either making food or storage of food. Plastids are further divided into groups as leucoplast, chromoplast and chloroplast. Chloroplast is involved in making food via photosynthesis. Leucoplast are colourless organelles mainly for storage and it is further grouped as amyloplast, elaioplast and aleuroplast. Chromoplast is an organelle that provides colour containing yellow or orange pigment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Carbohydrate of the cell membrane participates in
questions.solution: Carbohydrates are present on the outer surface of the cell membrane as a chain of sugar, glycoprotein, and glycolipids. Carbohydrates form only 1.5% of the component of the cell membrane and it helps in the cell to cell recognition as the cell surface receptors.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements about the plasma membrane is TRUE?
options: It allows selected molecules to pass into and out of the cell.
It is a rigid and unmoving layer of phospholipids and protein.
It is a solid layer of protein that protects the contents of the cell.
The plasma membrane of a bacterium has none of the same components as the plasma membrane of an animal cell.
questions.solution: Plasma membrane or the cell membrane which is made up of phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. It is a semipermeable membrane which allows ions and selected molecules to pass in and out of the cell. In bacteria, the cell wall is attached to the plasma membrane and plays the same role as a semipermeable membrane. The plasma membrane protects the cell from the outside environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant cell lacks
questions.solution: The plant cell is a eukaryotic composed of the cell wall, which is a rigid layer made of cellulose, pectin, and glycoproteins. It also has a semi-permeable cell membrane, nucleus, plastids, a central vacuole, Golgi apparatus, ribosomes, mitochondria, cytoplasm, chloroplast, etc. These cells lack centrioles and asters which are composed of the protein tubulin that is found in animal cells. The spindle formation is also not observed in plants, as they lack centrioles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phospholipid present in the cell membrane has
questions.solution: Phospholipids are lipid molecules made up of two fatty acids, glycerol and a phosphate group. They are components of the cell membrane and allow passage of selected substances in and out of the cell. The structure of these lipids is bilayered with a hydrophilic head (water-loving) and a hydrophobic tail (water-hating). Due to this property, they are also called amphipathic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In animal cell, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesized in
questions.solution: In animal cells, the lipid-like steroid hormone is synthesized by the smooth endoplasmic reticulum. Glyoxysome causes the breakdown of stored fats during seed germination by the glyoxylate cycle. Spherosomes are present in the plant cells which are involved in synthesis and storage of lipids. Lysosomes are suicidal bags which degrade the macromolecules by pocessing the lytic enzymes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The face of the Golgi apparatus receives the materials packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER is
options: both <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>
questions.solution: Golgi apparatus cisternae are spherical disc like structure present one on other and are curved. Curvature results in cis or convex face towards the nucleus and concave or trans face towards the cell membrane. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The human red blood cells are about _______ in diameter.
questions.solution: The human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter. These RBCs are the cells with hemoglobin and are involved in carrying the oxygen to the cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect match.
questions.solution: The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. In the chromoplasts fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present. This gives the part of the plant a yellow, orange or red colour. The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes?
questions.solution: Inclusion bodies: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells are stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm, e.g., phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules and glycogen granules. Gas vacuoles are found in blue green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Embryonal tissue of angiosperms contains:
questions.solution:
Chloroplast are organelles required for conducting photosynthesis.

Chromoplast provide colour to the cell.

Leucoplast are colourless plastids useful in storing carbohydrates and proteins. Embryonal tissue contain leucoplast as it helps in its growth and development by using the stored nutrients.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Intracellular space is divided into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal and extraluminal in:
questions.solution: The network of tiny tubular structures is scattered in the cytoplasm of the eukaryotic cell. This network is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This ER divides the intracellular space into luminal (inside the reticulum) and extraluminal (in the cytoplasm) compartments. If the reticulum has ribosomes on their surface, they are called rough endoplasmic reticulum and if no ribosomes are present then they are known as the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these scientists is not correctly matched with their contributions?
options: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell.
Matthias Schleiden studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the 'plasma membrane'
Rudolf Virchow first explained that cells divided and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells
questions.solution: Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist in 1838 while examining a large number of plants observed that all plants are made up of different cells. Theodore Schwann in 1839 who was a zoologist, studied animal cell and its types and observed that the cells in animals had a thin outer layer and today it is known as 'plasma membrane'

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the column I with column II
 
  Column I   Column II
a. Fat storage (i) Tubulin
b. Cilia (ii) Elaioplast
c. Mitochondria (iii) Contractile
d. Microfilaments (iv) Oxysomes
questions.solution:
Elaioplasts are one of the three possible forms of leucoplasts, sometimes broadly referred to as such.

The cristae of mitochondria has oxysomes . Oxysomes has a head and a stalk . head is called f1 particle and stalk is called f0 particles.

Tubulin refer either to the tubulin protein superfamily of globular proteins, or one of the member proteins of that superfamily. α- and β-tubulins polymerize into microtubules

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I (Sub-structures) with List II (Functions) and select the CORRECT answer using the codes given below the lists:
 
  List-I (Sub-structures)   List-II (Functions)
(A) Nucleosome (1) Cementing to keep neighbouring cells together
(B) Tubulin (2) A storehouse of oils and lipids
(C) Adhering junctions (3) Structural units of chromatin
(D) Elaioplasts (4) Protein units of microtubules
    (5) Oxidative phosphorylation
questions.solution:
DNA is wrapped histone proteins to form beads like structure called nucleosomes. This structure is further condensed to fit in a coiled helical structure called solenoid that on folding forms the chromatin fibre. Nucleosome forms the structural unit of chromatin fibre.

Microtubules found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells are made of polymers of protein, tubulin. Microtubules help with the structure and shape of the cell.

Tight junctions are a type of cell junctions found in epithelial tissue that help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

Elaioplasts are a type of leucoplast store oils and fats.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The least constancy of shape is exhibited by _______.
questions.solution: WBC’s are the phagocytic cells which performs phagocytosis by forming pseudopodia. Hence, they keep changing their structure.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the columns.
 
  Column I   Column II
1 Cristae (i) Flat membranous sacs in chloroplast
2 Cristernae (ii) Infoldings in mitochondria
3 Thylakoid (iii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus
questions.solution: The inner membrane of mitochondria is folded into a finger-like projection called cristae which increases the surface area for attachment of oxysomes. Cisternae are disc-like sac of the Golgi body. Thylakoid are membranous sac present in chloroplast which is stacked one on other to form grana.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cell which lacks cytoskeleton is
questions.solution: They are extremely minute, fibrous, and tubular structures that form the structural framework inside the cell. They occur only in eukaryotic cells. They maintain the shape of the cell, regulate orientation and distribution of cell transport and movement of cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Basal bodies are associated with the formation of:
questions.solution: The basal body is a microtubule-based protein structure located at the base of eukaryotic cilia. These organelles assemble cilia and flagella which are responsible for all the motility and sensory functions in the eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tonoplast is a membrane surrounding the
questions.solution: Large sap vacuole are present in plant cell only, they are surround by a single layered membrane called as tonoplast and the fluid present inside is called as tonoplasm or cell sap. Tonoplast is not a biomembrane and it facilitates the entry of ions into the tonoplasm against the concentration gradient from the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The type of ribosomes found in the cytoplasm of the organism responsible for causing typhoid and sleeping sickness are _____ and ____, respectively
questions.solution: Causative organism of typhoid is a bacterium Salmonella typhimurium. It is a prokaryote. The causative organism of sleeping sickness is Trypanosoma which is a protozoan. It is a eukaryote. Ribosomes are the granular structures composed of RNA and proteins. They are not surrounded by any membrane and are seen as dense particles under the electron microscope. Ribosomes found in cytoplasm of eukaryotic organisms are 80S and those in cytoplasm of prokaryotic organisms are 70S, where S is the coefficient of sedimentation and is a measure of the density and size of the ribosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Matthias Schleiden examined a sizable amount of plants and revealed the presence of
questions.solution: In 1838 Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist examined an outsized number of plant and observed that each one plants are composed of various sorts of cells which form the tissue of the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plasma membrane was discovered by whom and in which year?
questions.solution: Schwaan, 1839, a British zoologist studied different type of animal cell and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the plasma membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who concluded from his studies that the presence of a cell wall is a unique feature of plant cells?
questions.solution: Theodore Schwann (1839), a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the ‘plasma membrane’. He also concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells. On the basis of this, Schwann proposed the hypothesis that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Unicellular organism are capable of
options: performing the essential function of life
questions.solution: Unicellular organisms are capable of independent existence by performing the essential function of life and without organ and organ system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not true?
options: In plant outer layer in cell is cell wall and in animal cell membrane
Dence membrane bound nucleus and semifluid matrix cytoplasm is present in eukaryote cell only
Cytoplasm is the main area of cellular activities in plant and animal cells
questions.solution: Dense membrane bound nucleus in eukaryote cells only, semifluid matrix, cytoplasm is present in eukaryotic and prokaryotic both cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lysosomes are so-called as they have
questions.solution: Lysosomes are subcellular membrane-bound structure found in the eukaryotic cells. These vesicular structures are synthesized through the packaging process in the Golgi complex. Lysosomal enzymes are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum and are rich in all types of hydrolytic enzymes which help in digesting carbohydrates proteins lipids and nucleic acids therefore lysozyme act as the digestive system of the cell. The lysozyme organelles are also known as the suicidal bags of the cell because they cause lysis of the cell after the die.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In terms of permeability, the cell wall and plasmalemma are:
questions.solution: The cell wall present in the plant cells are made up of cellulose and is freely permeable to small molecules. The plasmalemma is the plasma membrane which is differentially permeable or semipermeable and allows the movement of selected molecules in and out of the cell. These membranes also function to protect the cell from the external environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: Mitochondria contain circular DNA, but chloroplasts lack it.
Chloroplasts contain circular DNA, but mitochondria lack it.
Neither mitochondria nor chloroplasts contain any DNA.
Both mitochondria and chloroplasts contain circular DNA.
questions.solution: Mitochondria also known as the powerhouse of the cell, has a small circular chromosome called the mitochondrial DNA which is passed through the egg cell from the mother to the offspring. The chloroplast, which are the plant organelles having the chlorophyll pigment and performs photosynthesis also contains small and circular DNA with many copies in it.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One key function of nuclear pores is to
options: aid in the production of new nuclei
allow cells to communicate with each other
allow molecules like proteins to move in and out of the nucleus
questions.solution: A nuclear pore is a protein channel found in the nuclear membrane. These pores are formed when there is a fusion of the two membranes in the nuclear envelope and functions to allow the transport of RNA and protein molecules from the nucleus to the cytoplasm and the DNA proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids from the cytoplasm to the nucleus. In short, they act as passageways for the proteins and other molecules to move in and out of the nucleus.
