Structure of a centriole.

(i) A centriole possesses a whorl of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin. It is absent in the center. Therefore, the arrangement is called a 9+0.
(ii) Each fibril is made up of three sub-fibres. Therefore, it is called triplet fibril named A, B, C.
(iii) The adjacent triplet fibrils are inter-connected by C-A proteinaceous linkers.
(iv) The centre of the centriole possesses a rod-shaped proteinaceous mass known as a hub. From the hub, nine proteinaceous strands are developed towards the peripheral triplet fibrils. These strands are called radial spokes.
(v) Due to the presence of peripheral fibrils and radial spokes, the centriole gives a cartwheel appearance.
(vi) There is no membrane boundary for a centriole, but it is surrounded by pericentriolar satellites, also known as massule.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Detailed membrane structure was studied only after the advent of ________
questions.solution: The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent of the electron microscope in the year 1950.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The eubacterial cellular part that is similar to a eukaryotic cell is ____
questions.solution:
Eubacteria are prokaryotic but are enclosed by plasma membrane like the eukaryotic cells. The composition and architecture of the plasma membrane remain the same for all cells.

Ribosomes are of 70S type in bacteria. The cell wall has peptidoglycan as the main component. The prokaryotes are devoid of the true nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: With respect to bacterial pilus, which of the following statements is not true?
options: They are made up of pilin protein.
They play an important role in movement.
questions.solution: Pilus or pili are surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made up of a special protein. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Statement 1: In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole.
Statement 2: In amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion.
options: Statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
Statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
questions.solution: In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole; hence their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm. In amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing other food particles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gas vacuoles are found in:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Gas vacuoles are the type of inclusion bodies (reserve material in the prokaryotic cells) which are found in cyanobacteria, purple sulphur bacteria and green bacteria and also in few floating aquatic forms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Choose the option that has only correct statements:
i. Inclusion bodies which are found in prokaryotic cells are not bounded by any membrane system.
ii. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
iii. Pili are the surface structures of the bacteria which may play a role in motility.
iv. The cell membrane of prokaryotes is structurally similar to the eukaryotes.
questions.solution: Besides flagella, pili and fimbriae are also surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein. The fimbriae are small bristle-like fibres sprouting out of the cell. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which among the following is true?
options: Plasma membrane helps in transportation of only water in and out of cell.
Plasma membrane helps in protein synthesis.
Plasma membrane helps in nucleic acid synthesis.
questions.solution: All cells are enclosed by a thin, film-like liable membrane called the plasma membrane or plasmalemma. The main function of the plasma membrane is to regulate the flow of materials into and out of the cell (osmoregulation). The membrane is selectively permeable.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a function of membranous extensions like vesicles and tubules?
options: Increase the surface area of the plasma membrane
questions.solution: A special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells. They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fluid mosaic model of plasma membrane shows that
options: quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
the lateral movement within the membrane is measured as its fluidity.
the fluid nature of membrane is important for growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis, cell division, etc.
questions.solution: Singer and Nicolson states that cell membrane is considered to be highly fluid. The integral proteins are capable of showing lateral diffusion in the lipid bilayer, studies with NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) and ESR (Electron Spin Resonance) technique indicate that lipid bilayer has many dynamic motional properties. Quasifluid nature of lipid enable lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer The fluid nature of membrane is important for growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion endocytosis, cell division etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The chief component of the middle lamella in plant cell is:
questions.solution: Middle lamella is the outer most layer of cell wall which functions as cementing layer present between two adjacent cells. It is made up of calcium pectate and magnesium pectate, but mainly calcium pectate which provides rigidity and hardness to the cell wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids is
questions.solution: The Golgi body is an organelle or a complex of vesicles found in the cytoplasm of most eukaryotic cells. It is responsible for packaging proteins into the vesicles before they are sent to their destination. These bodies perform the glycosyltransferase activity to add the glycans on lipid and proteins, therefore the glycoproteins and glycolipids are synthesized in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these cell organelles found exclusively in eukaryotes is not membrane bound?
questions.solution: The nucleolus, ribosomes, and centrioles are non-membrane bound cell organelles. Ribosomes are found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. The entire endomembranous system (ER, Golgi body, lysosome, vacuole), peroxisomes, cilia, flagella have a single membrane surrounding them. Mitochondria and nucleus are surrounded by two membranes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cell organelle is not present in plant cells but present in the animal cell?
questions.solution: Plant and animal cell are different as the former possess cell wall, plastids and a large central vacuole which are absent in animal cell. On the other hand, animal cell have centrioles which are absent in almost all the plant cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: As per the fluid mosaic model, how are phospholipid molecules arranged in a lipid bilayer?
questions.solution: According to the fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson, the major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged in a bilayer. Also, the lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards the inner part. This ensures that the nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
